images.title: Continental atlas
images.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: a finished visual-styling concept for Transit World Simulator, a proposed fictional enterprise simulation. Landscape 16:9, high resolution, exceptionally considered composition.
Visual language: editorial cartography meets a richly detailed simulation game. Clean warm-white interface, charcoal readable typography, sea-glass teal for selected objects, restrained ochre for attention. Soft mineral greens, blue water, warm gray architecture. Beautiful, calm, geographically credible, not cyberpunk. Thin precise map labels and small understated controls. The world occupies at least 85 percent of the canvas. No huge dashboard borders, no dense telemetry panels, no invented performance scores, no Google logo. Small footer "VISUAL CONCEPT · SYNTHETIC WORLD". All labels must be readable.
Primary request: A true high-altitude, straight-down continental map, with the usefulness and scale hierarchy of Google Maps terrain mode. Fill the frame edge to edge with a fictional continent across about 1800 kilometres, NOT a small island diorama. West coast at left with a vast estuary, interior fertile Heartland plain, long mountain spine across the north, dry red plateaus in the southwest, a heavily indented eastern coast and islands, and a volcanic southeastern peninsula. Hundreds of tiny cities and settlements at believable distances, fine rivers and tributaries, pale road networks and rail trunk lines, pale terrain shading and forest masses. Buildings and ships are too small to depict individually at this scale; cities are small circles and urban footprints.
Geographic labels: "CLEARING COAST" upper west, "HEARTLAND" center, "JAVA COAST" east, "RUBY BASIN" lower west, "GOPHER HIGHLANDS" north, "RUST PENINSULA" lower east. A thin teal selected freight corridor runs from Heartland across the eastern coastal mountains to a pin "Port of Beans" on the east-coast estuary. Dotted maritime routes continue beyond the frame. Regional boundaries use very faint dotted strokes.
Interface: compact floating search field top left "Search the world"; small pill beside it "Terrain   Freight   Places"; one modest floating card lower left headed "Heartland → Port of Beans" with "Explore corridor". Bottom right discreet plus/minus, north arrow, scale bar "200 km". Top right "World Commons". Huge sense of traversable distance, no horizon, no tilt, no giant landmarks, no glowing links, no floating slab. Beautiful highly legible atlas, not a fantasy board game.

Primary request: An expansive isometric city neighborhood on the east-coast Port of Beans estuary, which feels like zooming into a real map and then peeling back ONE city block. The occupied urban fabric stretches beyond all edges: streets, tram lines, rowhouses, civic buildings, offices, pocket parks, a rail station, working waterfront in the far upper right. Mid-rise European/industrial harbor character, lived-in, with trees and pedestrians. A central customs-house block is sliced open as a narrow archaeological trench revealing three stacked basement floors: a lower magnetic tape and mainframe room, middle server cabinets and bundled cables, upper modern data room. The rest of the city remains normal, above ground. No four isolated buildings on a floating geology slab.
Make the cutaway precise and delightful, a collectible miniature city with sunlight and rich material detail, not cartoon. Thin restrained leader labels on the excavation: "1978 · Mainframe", "2001 · Middleware", "2026 · Services"; upper street labels "Customs House", "Exchange Square", "Port of Beans". These dates are software history, not a time-travel control. A very small inspector top right "Software strata" with "Definition / Source / Observed". Bottom breadcrumb "World / Java Coast / Port of Beans / Customs House". Lower right scale bar "100 m". One selected cyan line follows the customs building's underground cable route to the waterfront, anchored in a city that continues far beyond this block. Keep the world overwhelmingly dominant.

images.title: Living port and facility
images.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.

No huge dashboard borders, no dense telemetry panels, no invented performance scores, no Google logo. Small footer "VISUAL CONCEPT · SYNTHETIC WORLD". All labels must be readable.
Primary request: A delightful, richly detailed high-oblique isometric miniature logistics game scene. Show Sector 04 warehouse as one building inside a large inhabited Port of Beans, not a detached room. Surround it with a canal and container quay at the top right, freight rail sidings on the left, street and tram stop in foreground, other warehouses receding at top, workers, bicycles, trees and a tiny lunch kiosk. The warehouse occupies the center half of the image; its roof is selectively removed to expose receiving, pallet racks, customs office, conveyors and dispatch. Coherent playable paths from trucks through receiving to shelves to the quay. Warm concrete, brick, dusty teal roofs, tiny ochre forklifts. Sunlight, craft, playful miniature realism, intricate but readable.
Inside the glass customs office a small green terminal glows. Bay B has an orderly visible queue waiting at a closed gate; Bay A has a forklift and small AMR carts using marked lanes. Tiny people remain safe behind striped crossings and barriers. One selected ochre forklift, labeled "Forklift-07", near the front opening is the camera anchor for a future first-person view; teal selection ring only around it. Labels "Bay B · Waiting", "Bay A · Loading", "Customs". Top breadcrumb "World / Java Coast / Port of Beans / Sector 04". Small lower-left pinned green-screen terminal card "Customs · Read only" with just "WB-90411   HOLD". Lower right modest action card "Forklift-07" and "Inspect / Enter POV". Scale bar "20 m". This should feel like an inviting miniature working world that is part of a much bigger city. No dramatic half-old half-futuristic split, no giant sci-fi core.

Primary request: First-person view from the driver's seat of a small ochre warehouse forklift in Sector 04 of Port of Beans, looking over two forks and a modest steering console. Intimate, tactile, beautifully art-directed simulation-game view, soft daylight through sawtooth factory windows. Pallet racks flank a broad aisle with cardboard cartons and scuffed concrete. At the far end an open loading door reveals a sunlit canal, quay crane and brick port buildings, connecting the interior to the wider world. A compact robot cart crosses behind a marked pedestrian barrier at middle distance. A target pallet stands near the right of the aisle. Maintain convincing physical proportions and visibility.
Very restrained augmented annotations: a fine teal outline on the target pallet, one dotted candidate path along the floor, and a white label "PLT-8841 · Selected". No giant cyan lattice over everything. Top left breadcrumb "Port of Beans / Sector 04 / Forklift-07". Top center clear mode pill "OBSERVE · Simulation paused". Bottom left a small floor-plan minimap titled "Sector 04" with the forklift position, and an adjacent compact terminal inset "Customs · Read only", "WB-90411   HOLD". Bottom center compact option pills "A · Dock route" and "B · Wait at gate", both visibly "Preview". Bottom right one deliberate control "Request control", with a subtle adjacent "No movement issued". Visually rich world, minimal chrome, readable calm game HUD. No weapons, no live actuation, no health bars, no unsupported success metrics.

images.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.

Visual language: editorial cartography meets a richly detailed simulation game. Beautiful, calm, geographically credible, not cyberpunk. Thin precise map labels and small understated controls. The world occupies at least 85 percent of the canvas. No huge dashboard borders, no dense telemetry panels, no invented performance scores, no Google logo. Small footer "VISUAL CONCEPT · SYNTHETIC WORLD". All labels must be readable.
Primary request: A cartographic modernization experiment workbench, showing the SAME large regional map in two synchronized equal side-by-side panes separated by a thin vertical rule. Straight-down terrain mapping, a 160-kilometre freight corridor from an agricultural inland city on the west through river valleys and low mountains to Port of Beans on an eastern estuary. In both panes the geography, roads, rivers, town positions and coastline are identical and remain fixed. Hundreds of small map details, beautiful quiet map rendering, no giant buildings. Title above left "A · Recorded baseline"; title above right "B · Candidate simulation". Tiny place labels on both: "Heartland Junction", "Customs", "Port of Beans". In left map, selected freight route ochre with three small labeled waiting clusters at junction and customs. In right map, selected route teal, one bypass candidate shown dashed, remaining bottleneck at quay shown with an ochre outlined square. Do not imply everything is solved.
At bottom, one slender comparison shelf across whole frame, headed "Same source basis · Same fault schedule", with three steps "Inspect → Simulate → Review", and clearly readable "Candidate only · Not applied". A small outlined control "Review proposed changes". Top left "Corridor laboratory"; top right "World Commons". Each map has a "20 km" scale bar. Retain place identity and scale; change overlays rather than replacing old architecture with futuristic towers. This is an inspectable experiment inside a vast world, not a before/after marketing diorama. High cartographic precision, elegant restrained typography.

images.title: Persistent world and local changes
images.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: a finished visual-styling concept for Transit World Simulator, a proposed fictional enterprise simulation. Landscape 16:9, high resolution, exceptionally considered composition.
Visual language: editorial cartography meets a richly detailed simulation game. Clean warm-white interface, charcoal readable typography, sea-glass teal for selected objects, restrained ochre for attention. Soft mineral greens, blue water, warm gray architecture. Beautiful, calm, geographically credible, not cyberpunk. Thin precise map labels and small understated controls. The world occupies at least 85 percent of the canvas. No huge dashboard borders, no dense telemetry panels, no invented performance scores, no Google logo. Small footer "VISUAL CONCEPT · SYNTHETIC WORLD". All labels must be readable.
Primary request: A vast continuous fictional continental night atlas seen from directly overhead, no curved orbital horizon. The same coherent geography as the day atlas: western estuary, immense inland Heartland plains, long mountain spine across the north, eastern Java Coast with Port of Beans on an estuary, southwestern red basin, southeastern Rust Peninsula. Hundreds of clustered city lights and narrow transportation networks across thousands of kilometres, large dark rural spaces and mountainous wilderness between cities, deep blue seas. The world continues beyond all four edges. Elegant satellite-at-night visual styling with muted indigo, sparse warm white lights, fine readable labels; no sci-fi energy dome or world-spanning upgrade wave.
Overlay a few bounded local application rollout footprints, geographically distinct polygons with non-color cues: a thin solid teal outline near the western metropolis tagged "Complete"; a hatched amber outline at Port of Beans tagged "Verifying"; a dashed white outline inland tagged "Queued". Most of the world is untouched. Fine shipping routes cross the sea. Keep actual lights separate from rollout state.
Minimal pale UI: top left search field "Find a place or installation"; top right "Persistent world · Observe". One modest bottom-left card "Port of Beans / Application rollout" with three short rows "Artifact · Staged", "Ownership · Awaiting handoff", "Data · Verification pending" and link "Inspect evidence". A narrow bottom timeline "Recorded history" with tick marks, no uptime or throughput claims. Bottom-right scale "200 km", plus/minus. Quiet, expansive, alive, a navigable night map, not a dashboard, miniature archipelago or glowing planet.
